newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigeria says to import oil until refineries fixed.
newsitem.headline: Nigeria says to import oil until refineries fixed.

text.p: Oil-producing Nigeria's renewed import of petroleum products to end an acute shortage of fuel in the country would continue until local refineries are back to satisfactory condition, an oil spokesman said on Wednesday.
The spokesman also said that the 33 cargoes of petroleum products to be immediately imported, which was announced on Tuesday, would arrive between this week and September.
"It is a continuos process pending the time we will get enough from domestic processing," a spokesman for the Pipelines and Products Marketing Company (PPMC) told Reuters.

PPMC, a unit of the Nigerian National Petroleum Corp (NNPC) is responsible for fuel supplies and its managing director Ibrahim Abubakar said on Tuesday that it had ordered three cargoes of fuel to come in between Tuesday night and Sunday.
"Importing is not limited to only this crisis period," said the PPMC spokesman, adding, "We want to ensure that the current crisis does not happen again."
The importation followed crisis talks by Nigeria's military rulers in the capital Abuja on Monday over the fuel crunch which paralysed businesses and caused severe hardship for commuters.
Allowing imports is a major climbdown by the military leader General Sani Abacha, who last September ordered a halt to imports and ordered NNPC to get local refineries to function.

Long queues for petrol were still visible at many pump stations in Lagos on Wednesday but many motorists said they expected the situation to ease because fuel was being delivered to the sales outlets.
Nigeria has four refineries capable of processing a total of 445,000 barrels per day of crude oil but they have been operating at a fraction of that because of their deteriorating condition.

According to PPMC, military ruler General Sani Abacha had also approved an immediate realistic reassessment of Nigeria's four refineries and pipelines in order to make funds available for their rehabilitation.
"At the moment, discussions are on with internationally acclaimed consultants who will undertake the reassessment of the refineries and the pipelines," Abubakar said on Tuesday.
The PPMC spokesman said serious efforts were now in place to ensure the refineries produce at their optimal capacity.
"As soon as PPMC management feels that domestic supply is okay it will take the appropriate decision on import," he said.
Nigeria has been criticised by its citizens in the last several weeks when fuel scarcity has stranded thousands of commuters at bus-stops and brought many cities to a standstill.
